title: India's Services Engine Just Hit Its Slowest Speed in Seventeen Months. The Hiring Freeze Is the Bigger Story.
excerpt: The HSBC India Services PMI fell to 57.4 in June as domestic demand weakened sharply and only 1% of firms added staff — a dramatic retreat from the hiring boom of April and May.
body:
India's services sector — the backbone of the economy, powering everything from IT outsourcing to financial services to hospitality — expanded at its slowest pace in seventeen months in June, according to data released on Friday.

The HSBC India Services Purchasing Managers' Index, compiled by S&P Global, fell to 57.4 from May's 59.8. While any reading above 50.0 still signals expansion, the direction of travel is unmistakable: the services engine that powered India through a global tech selloff and a Middle East oil crisis is losing steam.

"The loss of momentum points to more challenging market conditions and weaker demand, particularly at home," said Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC.

## Domestic Demand Is the Problem

The new business sub-index — the closest gauge of real demand — rose at its slowest pace since November 2023. Companies reported that competition was intensifying and market conditions were tightening, a sharp reversal from the demand surge that propelled the index to a six-month high just one month ago.

International demand offered some relief. New export orders grew at their fastest pace in three months, suggesting that global clients are still buying Indian services even as domestic appetite cools. But foreign orders alone are not enough to carry an economy where services account for more than half of GDP.

## The Hiring Picture Is Stark

The most concerning signal sits in the employment data. Only around 1% of surveyed firms reported hiring additional staff in June — a dramatic retreat from the robust job creation seen in April and May.

This matters enormously for the diaspora. India's $315 billion IT industry, which employs millions and feeds the pipeline of H-1B workers heading to the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom, has been under sustained pressure. Tata Consultancy Services, the country's largest software exporter, cut more than 12,000 jobs last year and has signalled it expects a broader industry slowdown in hiring.

For NRIs working in technology roles abroad, a weakening domestic services sector feeds directly into corporate belt-tightening at the companies that sponsor their visas, manage their projects and, increasingly, compete with AI agents for their roles.

## Inflation Eased, but Confidence Didn't

Input cost inflation dropped to a five-month low, with prices for electricity, food, fuel and transportation rising at a softer pace. Firms passed even less of that burden to clients, with the prices-charged sub-index falling to a seven-month low.

But cheaper inputs did not translate into optimism. Business confidence slumped to a five-month low, with firms citing competition, difficult economic conditions and rupee depreciation as their top concerns.

## The Composite Picture

The India Composite PMI — which combines services and manufacturing — slipped to its weakest since March. Output, new orders and employment all expanded at softer rates across the private sector.

Combined with the manufacturing PMI data released earlier this week, which showed factory activity at a four-year low, the message is consistent: India's private sector is cooling across the board.

The question now is whether the Reserve Bank of India's recent accommodative stance — it has cut rates by 75 basis points since February — can arrest the slide before it deepens, or whether the global trade uncertainty and AI disruption that companies keep citing in surveys will continue to weigh on confidence regardless of what monetary policy does.

For an economy that needs to create millions of jobs a year to absorb its young workforce, a services sector that is growing but not hiring is worse than a headline number of 57.4 might suggest.
